claims.text: Ab initio calculations using machine-learning-based exchange-correlation functionals can accurately predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed machine-learning-based exchange-correlation functionals incorporate experimental data.
The proposed calculations account for the effects of point defects on thermal conductivity.
The proposed calculations account for the effects of grain boundaries on thermal conductivity.
The proposed calculations account for the effects of oxygen impurities on thermal conductivity.
The modeled material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed approach is applicable from 0 to 200 K.
The proposed approach is applicable from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed calculations can accurately capture complex interactions among point defects, grain boundaries, and oxygen impurities.
Existing analytical predictions do not accurately account for interactions among point defects, grain boundaries, and oxygen impurities.
Capturing defect, grain-boundary, and oxygen effects will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
The proposed approach will reduce mean absolute error by at least 20% relative to existing analytical approaches.
The stated sample applicability is limited to HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
A deviation of more than 10% from experimental thermal-conductivity data would falsify the hypothesis.
